defs_parts: Eight labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Editor or docs: the term comes from the editor itself or its official documentation.
Outside source: the term comes from a source outside the course text.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: A trailer sells a game to a stranger, and a teaser only hints.
A logline explains the game in one sentence, and a tagline is only remembered.
Show real gameplay in the first five seconds, and put the logo last.
The peak lands on a strong beat, right after a quiet music drop.
Cut on action follows the motion, and cut on the beat follows the music.
An honest trailer shows only real play from the build, never planned features.
bookends.command: Quiz me on trailer terms with short cases about making a trailer for a game I built, one at a time. Use the terms trailer, teaser, logline, tagline, hook, climax, title card, call to action, cut on action and cut on the beat. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply.
checks: Check: each case is about a game trailer, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and said why its look-alike is wrong.
